notes.title: Rupert's Delivery is here!
notes.content: [h1]Rupert's Delivery has been released![/h1][previewyoutube="9pwJA4J17ik;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Patch 1.1 contains Rupert's Delivery. Using a special trusty trunk, guide Rupert through a new area and help him on his journey to deliver a parcel to a mystery recipient![/p][p]Accompanying this new content is a huge 70% discount for new players! Welcome and enjoy! (and tell your friends)[/p][h2]Additions and Changes[/h2][list][*][p]New Character: Rupert. Rupert's special ability is his extendable trunk, which he can use to grab onto hooks and then launch in one swift action.[/p][/*][*][p]New Area: The City. Over 50 levels of trunk slinging fun.[/p][/*][*][p]New Music: Rain or Shine, or Heights. A new track has been added to the game AND to the OST Songbird[/p][/*][*][p]The demo is BACK: Potential Kiopiok-ers can try before they buy. The demo is the newly rebalanced Shielded Plateau area.[/p][/*][*][p]Demo saves carry over to the full game. If you purchase after playing the demo, your progress will now carry over.[/p][/*][*][p]Rebalancing for Shielded Plateau: The difficulty ramped up too fast in this area, so adjustments have been made in the name of fun.[/p][/*][*][p]Rebalancing (NERF) to the first boss encounter: The Hungry Cat was too frustrating. Now, if you miss certain launches or jumps you aren't always punished with death. Many spikes have been removed and the level has been shortened. Halfway through the level there is now a switch that opens a shortcut; this will reduce the number of attempts needed to beat the level. The Hungry Cat now gives the player ~3 seconds head start before chasing; before it was about 1.[/p][/*][*][p]Improvements to D-pad controls[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]The idea for Rupert has been realized and has breathed new life into the whole game. I hope you enjoy the new content as much as I did making it.[/p][p][/p][p]-DevDave@HardieSoftworks[/p]

notes.title: Rupert's Delivery will launch on August 21!
notes.content: [h1]Get ready for a new free adventure in Kiopioke with an elephant named Rupert![/h1][previewyoutube="9pwJA4J17ik;full"][/previewyoutube][p]Rupert and his trusty trunk have been entrusted with delivering a package to an unknown recipient. Guide him through a new area called The City and meet some adversaries along the way.[/p][p]The patch brings some other changes as well, like the retuning of the Shielded Plateau area, especially the Hungry Cat encounter.[/p][p]The demo is returning so if you're a new player and you'd like to try before you buy, then give the demo a play! It's hard for me to believe that this adventure went from conception to release in less than two months![img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/277aa391ed8d9288a5ab5993d39b72b429bd6930.jpg"][/img]-DevDave@HardieSoftworks[/h3]

notes.title: Rupert's Delivery is new free content for Kiopioke, and it's coming soon!
notes.content: [h1]I am proud to announce new free DLC for Kiopioke called Rupert's Delivery. I plan to release it before the end of the summer.[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/6f9c8deac122d8a57a34aa041e5a2beeb0cf83f4.png"][/img][/p][h3]Rupert's Delivery is a short adventure where you play as Rupert, an elephant post officer. As Rupert, you must deliver a package to an unknown recipient high in the tower village of Skynest. Armed with a special extendable trunk, you must learn to climb and zip through a new zone called "The City".[/h3][p]The album Songbird will also receive an update which will include the new music from the free content.[/p][p]Rupert's Delivery was an idea I had in late June. Development has been smooth and honestly, quite fun. Rupert's mechanic is really satisfying and simple with depth for advanced players. The aim was to make a short, fun, and more accessible experience for players and I think I have succeeded. [/p][p]It is currently in alpha testing to provide some polish. Most of the additions past that are graphical and musical. Level design is mostly completed. Character mechanics and animations are pretty much done as well.[/p][p]I can't wait for you all to play it.[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/277aa391ed8d9288a5ab5993d39b72b429bd6930.jpg"][/img][/p][h1]-DevDave@HardieSoftworks[/h1][p][/p]

notes.title: Celebrating One Year of Kiopioke!
notes.content: [h2]Today marks one year since Kiopioke was released and I have some news to share![/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/73b098439469a6e5855e71e677199e89cbd5740f.png"][/img][/p][p]Since release I have been supporting the game with bug fixes and working on a lot of different game prototypes including [url="https://hardiesoftworks.itch.io/playconomy"]Playconomy[/url], [url="https://hardiesoftworks.itch.io/dreamshot-prototype"]Dream Shot[/url], and one other unannounced game.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/7fc747b193de830e057e150d4fa5dac8c837e2b6.png"][/img][/p][p][i]Dream shot is a multiplayer golf game that is inspired by Kirby's Dream Course. You can even build your own courses![/i][/p][p][/p][p]Kiopioke kept creeping into my thoughts, though. Recently I had a gameplay idea that I thought could work in Kiopioke, so I began exploring it. For the past few weeks I have been experimenting with the idea and creating the mechanics. Now the core mechanics are complete and I am happy to report that it feels great![/p][p]I think it has a place in Kiopioke sooooo,[/p][h2]I am pleased to announce that new free content is coming to Kiopioke![/h2][p]The new content will focus on a new mechanic and will feature new levels, a new playable character, and a new adventure. You can expect it to be about the size of 2 zones.[/p][p]I am currently in the "level design" phase of development. Once the levels are done there are graphics, music, sound effects, packaging, testing; the list is long but I want this development to be a quick as possible. It definitely won't take as long as the original release. I will update as I can and I can't wait for playtesting![/p][p][/p][h2]Finally, I want to thank everyone who has supported the game (and the music!). I am thankful for your feedback. I hope you are enjoying your summer. [/h2][p][/p][p]Keep in touch! I do smaller updates on [url="https://bsky.app/profile/davidhardie.net"]Bluesky [/url]and I will be sure to post more updates here on Steam soon![/p][p]Until then, here's a cute character.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/277aa391ed8d9288a5ab5993d39b72b429bd6930.jpg"][/img]-DevDave@HardieSoftworks[/p]

notes.title: What sets Kiopioke apart from other 2D platformers?
notes.content:
[h1][b]It’s the poke and launch mechanic![/b][/h1] I got the idea when playing Super Mario Odyssey. In that game, there is an enemy that Mario can possess called Pokio. Pokio has a beak that can poke into walls. Then the player can build tension and launch Pokio. The devs at Nintendo EPD Tokyo made the experience very satisfying, right down to the little chirping noise when holding a lot of tension. Daryl Talks games has a great video detailing the mechanic and character
[previewyoutube=zdsJETAo9nY;full][/previewyoutube]
In Mario Odyssey, the developers never linger too long with mechanics. It keeps things fresh, engaging, and exciting but it can leave players wanting more. I wanted more Pokio! So, I decided to make my own game centered around that mechanic.
My first attempt/prototype was originally called “Kiopioke” (current called Kiopioke PROTOTYPE on Itch.io). It was in a 3D space and used Unreal Engine’s built in physics to achieve an effective (and buggy) poke and launch.
[previewyoutube=JKhMQOdP3Ek;full][/previewyoutube]
It’s a bit floaty but it has some cool ideas that didn’t make it into the final game. For instance, you can poke into side walls! There’s a UI indicator that shows where the player “aim” is. There are even defeatable enemies!
When I decided to make a full game, I made a lot of design decisions that changed how the poke and launch would be coded. Instead of relying on built in physics systems, I created my own. The game took on much more of a Celeste vibe so the pacing was different. Jumping and dashing had to work together with the launch to feel good but not overpower the levels. The shape of Kiopioke also changed drastically as the design evolved:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/c1b9ec3e9d3400432ab0b6908376a260fe6979c6.gif[/img]
When Kiopioke successfully pokes into a wall, there is a dampening effect, like a spring. Players (especially speedrunners) can exploit this a bit to add some extra velocity to launches.
Players are given the freedom to aim in any direction (while using a gamepad). When players release their aiming direction, the character launches. The high level logic is:
1.	Players aims
2.	If the controls get close enough to “0” (or no input from player) then the character will launch.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/6ae7fa28190ef80a8cfa9a74315bce1a5d4feef4.gif[/img]
This makes for a satisfying launch. I made it much snappier and quicker than our friend Pokio because I think it works better for this Celeste-like game. It feels awkward to jump and dash and then wait a second while building tension. Instead the player can launch the character very quickly.
Launching feels good and is an awesome tool for the player, but I thought there could be more to the mechanic. In later levels, the player has to hang on to walls and dodge obstacles.
[previewyoutube=f8V7ZbuClho;full][/previewyoutube]
So I simply added functionality that prevents the character from launching if the player holds down a button. It adds a new dimension to the poke.
I’m incredibly happy with how it turned out. But my early players weren’t always so thrilled. Why? Well, I believe it’s because everybody wants to control it differently. I use the R-Stick to control launches, but many people preferred using the L-Stick, which is also used for movement. Giving players the option to control it the way they felt comfortable was really important to me; it’s gotta feel good! Once I added these options, players were very positive about their launch experiences.
I originally wanted to expand upon the Pokio mechanic from Mario Odyssey. I believe I have done so, and pretty soon you can see for yourself. Kiopioke pokes… and launches…on July 18th.

notes.title: Beta testing is upon us! Here are some important comments from playtesters and m
notes.content:
The full game is being beta tested and I have been getting awesome feedback from players on what is working and what still isn't. At this point, it is relatively small tweaks but I wanted to touch on a few of the comments from the testers so far. If you are interested in joining the conversation, join the Discord. The game releases on July 18 on Steam and, of course, Itch!

----------

[i]This first comment is relevant to parts of the game not included in the demo. Certain platforms and walls can move and affect player momentum.[/i]

[b]“The only thing that I really disliked throughout the game was the momentum physics. When you are on a fast moving platform and flick off of it, it gives you a boost. But the boost you get seems completely random, and I find it so annoying when rooms require multiple momentum jumps that feel random.”[/b]

I really want the gameplay to feel good and not random, so I hated that it felt that way for you. So I did something about it and now platforms and walls have more “velocity forgiveness” when launching or jumping.

Details: If you jump or launch near the end of a platform/wall path, the velocity passed to the player will not immediately go to zero. This logic was coded into Synchro platforms (the ones that move when you dash) but it didn’t translate properly to other walls and platforms; until I did it a different way.

Here’s a table that maybe explains it better. The scenario is that a platform/wall comes to an abrupt stop. So what velocity should it pass to the player for their jump? (numbers completely made up for simplicity)

Old version:
Time	Platform/wall velocity	Velocity passed to player
0	        300	                                300
1	        300	                                300
2	        0	                                0
New Version
Time	Platform/wall velocity	Velocity passed to player
0	        300	                                 300
1	        300	                                 300
2	        0	                                 250
3	        0	                                 200
4	        0	                                 150
…		

This still rewards players for a well-timed jump but doesn’t absolutely punish players when they miss just a bit. I will probably need to tweak some parameters of this but so far I like how it keeps things a little more consistent. It DEFINITELY makes Skynest-Unseen_04 more fun.


[i]This comment has some relevance to the demo, you can see this change when selecting SP_006, Bullet's room.[/i]
[b]
“Just a QOL thing, can you give some kind of indication of important things on the level selector to indicate if some characters are there or the entrance to a secret bonus level area”[/b]

Two ways I am addressing this problem:
[list]
[*]Adding signs that allow the player to teleport to characters. Sometimes there are NPCs that have this in their dialogue, but I think it’s good to be consistent and add the signs as well.  In the Cliffs, for example, there is a sign near the barrel that will take you back to the level with Olivia and Schroeder. These signs didn’t always exist everywhere so I have added them in.
[*]The suggestion to add a visual cue on the level selector is a good one. Here’s what it looks like:
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/678c6a3e28d7951b287877cb8665f4e1642b8790.png[/img]

[b]“Probably my main concern with the game is the ceiling for creative expression with the movement, I hate to just make comparisons but take a platformer like celeste for example. No matter what the level design is, you can always string together your moves to perform tricks, gain speed or do skips etc. but with kiopioke im not sure if how the current movement physics work really allows for that kind of expression, seeing as im not sure if you can gain more speed than your base dash without moving platforms”[/b]

This design decision is partly that I am not a skilled enough coder to make what EXOK made. Supermanning around the level in Celeste is an amazing skill that is reserved for a very small percentage of players so I didn’t pursue it; I was never going to be able to replicate Celeste in that area. I tried to make it so that there are a lot of levels that can be done in different ways, and that is how the personality of the player shows. I was watching a friend play last night and even after all the players I’ve watched, he still had different ways of finishing demo levels that I had not seen before.

[b]“A much smaller nitpick is it can be a little weird to try and walljump, as it can sometimes feel like im "stuck" to a wall and jump upwards when im trying to jump away. could be a skill issue lol”[/b]

Here is how it is set up:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/8b45690540727057a1edf206c22c4d7c84a98956.png[/img]

I would have to double check but I believe this is different than Celeste, which only allows jump upwards when the input is upwards. I made this choice based on really early alpha feedback from a much smaller group of players; when I watched them play, they would attempt to jump upward and be surprised when they jumped to the side. Not sure what the solution is or if there is a clear cut one here.

----------

That's all for now! You can wishlist on Steam if you'd like or follow me on Itch.io.

notes.title: Demo has been updated to 1.04!
notes.content:
Hello everyone and thanks for playing the demo. I have been gathering feedback from streamers, posters, speedrunners, and viewers and applied some changes and fixes to the demo which I hope will make your experience more enjoyable.

The biggest change is how the poke/aim/launch mechanic controls now. By default, it will use the movement controls. Before this, separate controls were used for this mechanic. If you prefer the old way, don't fret! There is now an option to use the old method:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44796076/3c4ba08a6eeaefef7606372b1e4b0feef0f0c426.png[/img]

Other changes/fixes:
[list]
[*]The cat will not stop to talk after the first pass in level 049 (known as the cat level)
[*]Level 049 (known as the cat level) has been rebalanced and now has more places to grab on to.
[*]When stamina runs out there is now an audio and visual indicator
[*]Updated translations
[*]Fixes for save game objects; this should improve object behaviour when loading levels
[/list]

I'm hard at work fleshing out the rest of the game. As I iterate and make improvements I will continue to update the demo, so your feedback really helps! Join the [url=https://discord.gg/ETEjjuqzfG]Discord[/url] and let me know your thoughts on the game.

-hydrok
